title: PART 3 - The AI label didn't cost Next Fest games followers. I tried hard to prove otherwise
author: Dream_Ep
selftext:
Third and last one on AI in the October Next Fest (1 in 3 games had a disclosure, mostly for art)

So, the question everyone kept asking: does the label scare players away? :D

I compared follower growth during the fest, Oct 19 to Oct 29, only between games of the same size, meaning the same number of Steam followers before the fest. And the games with a disclosure didn’t grow slower. They actually grew a bit faster, in every size group

Under 50 followers, median +43% vs +30%  
200 to 499, +23% vs +17%  
500 to 2K, +17% vs +10%

Among games that started with 10 to 49 followers, 17% of the disclosing ones doubled, vs 10% of the others

Honestly I didn’t believe it so I tried to kill it haha

Games with the label ship more languages (6 vs 3 in the median, hello AI translation). Same number of languages? still there..  
With or without Chinese on the page? still there..  
Tag by tag, they’re ahead in 16 of the 16 biggest tags among small games, and 12 of 14 between 50 and 499 followers..  
And it’s medians per game, so it’s not a couple of big hits pulling everything up

The one thing I couldn’t kill is page age. Someone on the first post pointed out that AI devs tend to be newer and move faster, and fresh pages grow faster anyway. I can only date a small part of the pages, but on the ones older than 6 months the gap just disappears. Small sample so I can’t say much more, but it might be a big part of the story. Same at the top btw, of the 28 games above 10K followers at least 17 had their page up for over a year before the fest

And yeah “no disclosure” doesn’t mean “no AI”, lots of you said it on the first post and you’re right, some studios just don’t declare it. So this compares games that put the label on their page with games that didn’t, nothing more

Before anyone grabs a pitchfork, these are followers. Not sales, not reviews. Wishlists aren’t public so followers are the closest thing I can compare across thousands of games, and players can still hate it in the reviews later ! :D

Why does it happen? no idea really. My guess is the disclosure sits at the very bottom of the page and nobody scrolls that far when you’re clicking through 40 demos in an evening. And devs using AI might just ship more stuff around the game too (languages, trailers, capsules). So it’s not “use AI to grow”, more like the label alone didn’t sink anyone during the fest

Above 2K followers there are only 17 games with a disclosure, so grain of salt on that end. No game names as usual..!

I’m building NextWishlist, it tracks this kind of stuff for your own game and its niche every day. Link in the comments if you’re curious!

comments.body:
For the curious ones: I’m working on NextWishlist because most of us end up guessing whether our wishlists are “good” or not.

The idea is to see where your game stands in its niche, compared to games like yours, and get advice that actually fits your situation hehe

It’s a closed beta for now and I’m not selling anything, it’s free, I’m just looking for devs to test it and tell me what’s wrong with it. If that sounds useful to you, you can join the waitlist here: [https://nextwishlist.com](https://nextwishlist.com/?ref=igwai2) And if you’d just rather ask me questions, my DMs are open, happy to chat ! ;)

And since this whole thread is about it: yes, I use AI to build the site, like pretty much every dev in 2026. My actual job is data, not visuals. Collecting the Steam data, checking the numbers and trying to break my own results, that’s the part I do myself.. I'm building a tool that use that kind of data to help indie dev to market their game that's all ! :D

comments.author: WWEtrump
comments.body: the page age part is the interesting bit, makes sense that a fresh page grows faster just because it's new. i'm sitting on no store page at all, still waiting on steamworks approval, so this is useful. did you see any pattern in how many followers a page had before the fest versus how it grew? curious what a healthy number even looks like at launch

replies.author: Dream_Ep
replies.body:
Yeah, there’s a clear pattern..!  
In percent, small pages grow way faster. Under 50 followers the median was around +30 to 40% during the fest, 500 to 2K more like +10 to 17%. But that’s percent: a bigger page still gains more followers in raw numbers, it just looks smaller relative to where it started 

For you, the page age thing is honestly the useful part. Get the page up as soon as Steamworks lets you..! Every month it’s live before your fest or launch is time to collect wishlists, and you get that “fresh page” boost at a moment you choose ;)

As for a healthy number at launch, it depends a lot on the genre. What’s great for a card game can be weak for a cozy sim, which is why I compare games within their niche instead of using one magic number. There are free guides on the site about this (link in my first comment), no signup needed. And if you want, NextWishlist can follow your page from day one once it’s live, still a free closed beta!! :D

replies.author: WWEtrump
replies.body: yeah the percent thing is sneaky. a 2k page jumping looks huge and a 200k page doing the same absolute numbers looks dead

replies.author: Dream_Ep
replies.body:
What do you mean? If there’s an agenda it’s not really hidden, it’s the link in the first comment of every post. I’m building a tool for indie devs and data like this is what I do..?

The 4 posts were planned one per day from the start, I spoiled the next one in the comments each time. And no, I’m not pushing AI either way.. The label not hurting followers surprised me too, which is why half the post is about what it doesn’t prove

For the graphs, yeah I tried something different from usual this time as I said before ! And for the writing, English isn’t my first language (French here), so I do get help polishing it but everything is from me!
